summary.headline: Bharat Forge Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 18.7% YoY to INR4,640 crores, but EBITDA margin was 16.2% after a ~160 bps input-cost hit.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue rose 11.5% YoY to INR2,347 crores and EBITDA rose 4.5% to INR614 crores at a 26.2% margin, which management said absorbed about 160 bps of energy, input and logistics cost increases (normalised margin near 28%). Consolidated EBITDA was INR752 crores (up 10.3%). Overseas performance was mixed: Europe was EBITDA-positive, while US steel operations lost money after a multi-month press breakdown. Management announced a fundraise of up to INR2,500 crores for growth capex and said FY27 should be very good, with FY28 also strong.

financial_highlights.metric: Standalone EBITDA margin normalised for input-cost hit

financial_highlights.value: INR24 crores (consultancy for BF CDP restructuring)
INR461 crores / EBITDA loss of INR4 crores

segments.name: Forging (India/Global)
segments.commentary: New orders of INR522 crores in the quarter. Management says aerospace revenue is about INR400 crores and expected to double in about two years.

segments.name: Defence (Kalyani Strategic Systems)
segments.commentary: New orders of INR681 crores; order book INR11,196 crores at quarter end. Strong operating performance from higher realisations and better mix; steady-state margin target 22-23%. Won large Kolkata-class marine gas turbine generator order, its largest naval order to date.

segments.name: Ferrous castings (JS Auto Cast)
segments.commentary: Revenue and EBITDA grew 27% and 30% YoY; new orders about INR150 crores. Management aims to triple revenue versus acquisition-time level, with run-rate reached by end of this year.

segments.name: Bharat Forge CDP (Germany steel)
segments.commentary: Restructuring on track, targeted to complete by end-calendar 2027; EUR 30 million impact taken, with cash outflow expected only after 12 months. Closure timeline is Q3 CY2027.

segments.name: US operations
segments.commentary: EBITDA loss of INR4 crores on INR461 crores revenue, due to breakdown of several presses in steel operations, with recovery expected in Q2. Longer-term targets: steel EBITDA about 12%, aluminium 15-16%, hoped for next year.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 expected to be better than Q1, helped by customer price increases and volumes, and by non-recurrence of Q1 one-time items.
Margin recovery expected to be gradual; margin per ton to return to normal levels as cost pass-through to customers is recovered.
Overall organic capex about INR1,800 crores in India (forging, machining, heat treatment, ring rolling), to be completed over about 18 months; asset turnover expected above 1.5x.
Fundraise of up to INR2,500 crores for growth capex, including an energetics plant in Andhra Pradesh; instrument yet to be finalised.
Management expects FY27 to be a very good year, with H2 stronger, and FY28 also strong.
Defence margin target of 22-23% on a steady-state annual basis.
Manpower back to about 70-75% of normal; Maharashtra energy price hike remains a concern.
Management expects to recover energy and logistics cost increases from customers over time.
capex_capacity: Organic India capex of about INR1,800 crores spread across forging, machining, heat treatment and ring rolling, for both auto and non-auto applications.
Ring mill in Baramati expected to start in Q4 FY27; new Baramati forging facility to serve high-horsepower engine and power-gen customers.
New defence facility to enter serial production this year for ATAGS and CQB carbine deliveries.
Third new mega site in Odisha: environmental approvals expected by end of this year; first plant about 2.5 years after approvals.
New K Drive plant planned in northern India for a major customer.
Andhra Pradesh energetics/propellant plant is modular; licence applied for and not yet granted.
demand_pricing: North America demand strong on corporate capex, construction, mining, data centre and power systems; US steel margins to recover once plant operations normalise.
Management expects defence exports to need government support (e.g., export financing) and inbound interest is not quantified.
Semiconductor target of about USD 30-40 million business in two years organically, with machining facilities to nearly double it.
Data centre/energy business expected to double in four years, with long-term contracts in place.
Aluminium tariffs in the US (50% on raw aluminium from Canada) are hurting US margins; management says it is riding this out without cash losses.
Price increase discussions with customers under way; India demand described as fairly strong and Europe CV strong, Europe PV not as strong.

qa_highlights.question: Asset turns, margins and returns for the new businesses, and the overall capex plan for FY27/28?
qa_highlights.answer: Organic India capex is about INR1,800 crores, with asset turnover above 1.5x and accretive margins; business is already tied up for initial ramp-up.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise equity when the balance sheet is strong, and is the INR2,500 crore raise over and above the INR1,800 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wants to keep about INR2,000 crores of cash on balance sheet and sees M&A opportunities in India (JS Auto Cast, K Drive cited). The INR2,500 crore raise funds the current capex and leaves room for further growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 22-23% margin guidance company-wide?
qa_highlights.answer: No, it applies to the defence business on a steady-state annual basis.

qa_highlights.question: Will the cost pass-through reverse margins immediately?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins will improve gradually. Recoveries add to both revenue and cost, so reported margin will look better but not fully return to 28% immediately; per-unit margin will recover.

qa_highlights.question: Why was domestic CV/PV growth below industry, and what caused the Q1 supply challenges?
qa_highlights.answer: Mid-quarter steel labour and supply issues, plus fuel switching during the energy disruption. Management says these were overcome.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the CDP restructuring and its orders?
qa_highlights.answer: The CDP entity will cease to exist after restructuring; a sizable part of its orders will move to India at good margins, while some are being phased out.

risks_watch: Recovery of energy and logistics cost increases from customers; timing of margin normalisation towards 28%.
US steel plant restart in Q2 and 50% US tariff on raw aluminium affecting US margins.
ATAGS approval timing (FOPM) and the delivery ramp, with a few weeks of delay already flagged.
Odisha mega-site environmental clearance, expected by end of this year.
Execution of the INR2,500 crore fundraise instrument and the INR1,800 crore capex programme.
Manpower availability at 70-75% of normal; Maharashtra energy price hike.
INR330 crore manpower redundancy cost to be paid over 6-12 months, plus CDP restructuring cash outflow after 12 months.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term growth and FY27-28 demand, but candid that Q1 was affected by energy, labour and US plant disruptions. Management was vague on the Odisha project, the new M&A targets and the fundraise instrument, and declined to quantify US losses.
key_quotes: So this capex is going to be -- this capex is something that we will complete over the next 18 months and it will give us a high capital output ratio as well as good margins
I would say so, yes. I would say based on what we see right now, I think '28 should also be a strong year.
The margins are all a result of the product mix. But as we have mentioned, the margins on a steady state annual basis we are targeting in the 22% to 23% or so range.

growth.why: Management says FY27 will be a very good year with H2 stronger and FY28 also strong, backed by an INR11,196 cr defence order book, INR1,800 cr organic India capex (asset turnover above 1.5x) and aerospace/data-centre doubling targets, though no explicit FY27 revenue growth % was given and the Q1 margin was hit by ~160 bps of input costs.
